rationale: C17 plausibly supplied a material template for the child’s appeal to continue a conference-generated prevention campaign through state and community action. Both texts move from recognition of a national social problem, to a recent conference and its objectives, to mobilization of organizations and individuals, and finally to continued local action and education. C03 is close in correspondence format, addressee, and appreciative tone, but lacks the child’s conference-based public-campaign machinery. C23 parallels the emphasis on prevention education and coordinated public-private effort, though less closely than C17.

shared_material.child_excerpt: so many organizations and individuals gave such wholehearted support to this cause
shared_material.parent_excerpt: many important agencies, governmental and private, national and local, and individuals the country over, banded together
shared_material.explanation: Both mobilize a broad coalition of public and private organizations and individuals around a prevention campaign.

shared_material.child_excerpt: supporting the programs which you helped our states and communities launch
shared_material.parent_excerpt: immediate action in every State and community ... continuing community action
shared_material.explanation: The child adapts C17’s state-and-community implementation framework to fire prevention.

shared_material.child_excerpt: We must carry forward the program of education ... Only by these means can we hope to achieve the full objectives adopted at the conference
shared_material.parent_excerpt: to respond promptly to the call of the national Conference ... to study ... the recommendations of the National Conference ... in reaching the objectives of the national Conference
shared_material.explanation: Both connect continued educational or local action to objectives and recommendations produced by a national conference.
